fallback_used: Same-process Next.js smoke server with HTTP fetch
validation_method.notes: Interactive browser automation was not available in this session. Validation focused on build integrity, deterministic planner behavior, and successful rendered smoke output.

checks.name: Typography contract matches the new design direction
checks.evidence: layout.tsx now loads Noto Sans JP and Oswald together, globals.css exposes the numeric font variable, and page.module.css applies Oswald to fare, route, and metric callouts while keeping Japanese hierarchy on Noto Sans JP.

checks.name: Bauhaus plus neo-brutalist styling replaced the older parchment-only shell
checks.evidence: page.module.css now uses warm off-white surfaces, red/blue/yellow accent geometry, stronger black borders, harder shadows, and tighter card radii across the planner, result folio, and supporting sections.

checks.name: Interactive motion matches the new hover and reveal requirements
checks.evidence: Buttons and tiles now use a 0.3 second lift-hover treatment, and page.tsx plus page.module.css add staggered spring-like reveal behavior for major sections with a reduced-motion fallback.

checks.name: Planner preview distinguishes stay countries from gateway expansion before search
checks.evidence: The planner form now shows a dedicated preview that separates selected stay countries, auto-expanded gateway countries, and the total airport pool so the search scope is explicit before the comparison runs.

checks.name: Gateway-pair planner behavior remains intact
checks.evidence: npm run test:planner passed without changes to the planning logic, confirming that flexible months, stay windows, gateway expansion, and two-ticket outputs still work.

checks.name: App still renders and builds after the design refresh
checks.evidence: npm run smoke and npm run build both passed after the Bauhaus Motion Refresh changes. build was run separately from smoke to avoid the known .next concurrency conflict.

acceptance_criteria_results.criterion: The shell feels materially more geometric and confident than the prior Grand Tour Ledger dossier treatment.
acceptance_criteria_results.evidence: The shell now uses a Bauhaus-leaning neo-brutalist palette, stronger borders, harder shadows, and a less parchment-only presentation across the planner and results UI.

acceptance_criteria_results.criterion: Numeric callouts and route codes visibly use Oswald while Japanese editorial copy uses weighted Noto Sans JP.
acceptance_criteria_results.evidence: layout.tsx loads both Noto Sans JP and Oswald, and the UI applies Oswald to fares, route codes, and metrics while retaining weighted Noto Sans JP for Japanese hierarchy.

acceptance_criteria_results.criterion: Buttons hover with a soft lift and stronger shadow instead of abrupt color swaps.
acceptance_criteria_results.evidence: The updated page.module.css hover treatment uses a 0.3 second lift, scale, and shadow increase on the main interactive controls.

acceptance_criteria_results.criterion: Major sections reveal from below with staggered spring-like motion without harming usability.
acceptance_criteria_results.evidence: page.tsx and page.module.css now use staggered reveal timing with spring-like easing and a reduced-motion fallback, while smoke and build validation still pass.

next_actions: Add live fare enrichment in Sprint 8 without breaking the current numeric typography and result-card hierarchy.
Perform a true browser-based visual QA pass when automation is available so spacing, animation timing, and mobile composition can be verified beyond smoke rendering.
Consider expanding the gateway preview into a richer before-search route diagram once live data work begins.
